title: Carafe not sensed
shortDescription: Magnetic carafe sensor does not detect carafe.
fullDescription:
Cuisinart drip coffee makers (DCC, DGB series) use a magnet on the carafe and reed switch in the base to detect carafe presence. If misaligned, missing magnet, or failed reed switch, brewing is blocked.

Clean the base contact area and verify the carafe magnet is intact.

fixSteps.title: Reseat carafe
fixSteps.instruction: Push fully into warmer plate.

fixSteps.title: Verify magnet
fixSteps.instruction: Check bottom of carafe for magnet.

faq.a: Must have correct magnet placement.

title: Clean indicator illuminated
fullDescription:
The Clean light indicates calcium buildup. Run vinegar or descaler cycle to clear.

Duration is roughly 30 minutes; reset is automatic on completion.

fixSteps.title: Run clean cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Fill to MAX with 1:1 vinegar:water, press CLEAN button.

faq.a: Every 60 brews or monthly.

title: Temperature too low / too high
fullDescription: On programmable models with temperature sensors, this error fires if water temp is below 180F or above 205F. Heavy scale is the usual cause.

fixSteps.title: Descale
fixSteps.instruction: Run vinegar cycle twice.

faq.a: Likely scale - descale first.

title: Brewing too slow
fullDescription: Slow brewing is usually caused by mineral buildup restricting the heating tube or pump path.

fixSteps.title: Descale
fixSteps.instruction: Vinegar cycle.

faq.a: Helps slow buildup.

title: Unit will not power on
fullDescription: Failed thermal fuse, blown internal fuse, or dead control board.

fixSteps.title: Try different outlet
fixSteps.instruction: Test on known-good outlet.

fixSteps.title: Check thermal fuse
fixSteps.instruction: Disassemble base, test fuse continuity.

faq.a: Often cheaper to replace under $100 unit.

title: Grind & brew grinder jammed
fullDescription: On DGB series, beans or stones can jam the grinder.

fixSteps.title: Empty hopper
fixSteps.instruction: Remove all beans and inspect.

faq.a: Yes, bypass grinder via setting.

title: Water leaking from base
fullDescription: Leaks usually come from a cracked reservoir tube, failed gasket, or clogged shower head causing overflow.

fixSteps.title: Inspect reservoir
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and check for cracks.

faq.a: Replace reservoir; epoxy unsafe.

title: Brew button does not start cycle
shortDescription: Power on but no brew when pressed.
fullDescription: Likely a stuck Brew button, locked-out timer, or carafe sensor.

fixSteps.title: Cancel Auto-On
fixSteps.instruction: Press Auto-On to disable scheduled brew.

faq.a: Unplug 5 minutes.

title: Clean indicator
fullDescription: Descaling needed. This is a common diagnostic indication on Cuisinart coffee machines. Most issues can be resolved with cleaning, reset, or part replacement following the brand's service procedure.

fixSteps.title: Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug coffee machine for 60 seconds, then plug back in.

fixSteps.title: Clean
fixSteps.instruction: Clean any sensors/contacts indicated by the brand's manual.

fixSteps.title: Test
fixSteps.instruction: Run a normal cycle and verify error does not return.

whenToCallPro: If problem persists after cleaning and reset, professional service may be needed.

faq.a: Resolve the error first to avoid worsening the issue.
If under warranty, contact manufacturer before DIY repair.

title: Self-Clean Cycle Reminder
shortDescription: CL light indicates a cleaning cycle is due — distinct alert pattern on DCC and SS series.
fullDescription: CL alert appears after roughly 100 brew cycles. The internal calcium counter triggers it on hard-water settings.

fixSteps.title: Clean cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Fill reservoir 2/3 vinegar 1/3 water, press CLEAN, wait for completion.

fixSteps.title: Rinse
fixSteps.instruction: Fresh water, run two full brew cycles.

faq.a: Every ~100 brews; sooner with hard water.

title: Programming Mode Issue
shortDescription: PROG indicator stuck on or programmed brew time not triggering.
fullDescription: PROG sets the auto-brew schedule. If the indicator stays lit but auto-brew does not start, check time setting and AM/PM.

causes.cause: PROG not committed (must press PROG twice)

fixSteps.title: Reset clock
fixSteps.instruction: Set HOUR/MIN with attention to AM/PM.

fixSteps.title: Reprogram
fixSteps.instruction: Hold PROG, set time, press PROG again to confirm.

videoSearchQuery: Cuisinart PROG auto brew not starting

faq.a: Often AM/PM set wrong or PROG not double-pressed.

title: Charcoal Water Filter Replacement
shortDescription: FILTER alert reminds the user to replace the charcoal water filter cartridge.
fullDescription: Cuisinart machines with a built-in charcoal filter alert every 60 days. A clogged filter can also reduce flow.

fixSteps.title: Replace filter
fixSteps.instruction: Remove holder, slide in new charcoal filter cartridge.

fixSteps.title: Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Hold CLEAN for 3 seconds to reset filter timer.

faq.a: Every 60 days or 60 brews.

title: E1 Sensor Fault
shortDescription: E1 error indicates a temperature sensor fault on premium DGB grind-and-brew models.
fullDescription: E1 means the heater thermistor reading is out of range. The machine disables heating to prevent damage.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug 5 minutes, plug back.

fixSteps.title: Service
fixSteps.instruction: If E1 returns, contact Cuisinart support.

whenToCallPro: If E1 persists after power cycle.

faq.a: Power cycle is the only DIY step; further repair needs service.

title: E2 Heater Fault
shortDescription: E2 error indicates the heater is not reaching target temperature in time.
fullDescription: E2 triggers when the heater fails to hit the brewing temperature within the expected time, suggesting heater failure or scale buildup.

fixSteps.title: Descale
fixSteps.instruction: Run vinegar clean cycle.

fixSteps.title: Service
fixSteps.instruction: Heater replacement if descale does not fix.

faq.a: Sometimes — try first before assuming heater failure.

title: Bean Hopper Empty
shortDescription: Grind-and-brew models alert when the bean hopper is too low for selected cup count.
fullDescription: DGB models include a bean sensor; if beans are below threshold, the grinder will not run.

fixSteps.title: Refill
fixSteps.instruction: Add fresh beans.

fixSteps.title: Tap to break bridge
fixSteps.instruction: Light tap on hopper to settle beans.

faq.q: Can I leave beans in hopper?
faq.a: For best flavor, only fill what you will use in 1-2 weeks.

title: Bean Hopper Lid Open
shortDescription: The bean hopper lid sensor reports the hopper is open during brew.
fullDescription: DGB models require lid closed during grind. Lid-open prevents bean spill and grinder injury.

fixSteps.title: Close firmly
fixSteps.instruction: Press lid until click.

faq.q: Why does it say lid open?
faq.a: Lid not fully seated or sensor weak.

title: Carafe Not Detected
shortDescription: Carafe sensor reports missing carafe — alternative pattern from base CARAFE alert.
fullDescription: DCC and SS-15 models detect carafe via micro-switch. Improper placement or worn switch triggers alert.

fixSteps.title: Reposition carafe
fixSteps.instruction: Slide back fully under brew basket.

fixSteps.title: Inspect switch
fixSteps.instruction: Look for stuck pin behind brew basket.

faq.a: Single-cup uses a separate position, not the carafe sensor.

title: Clock Reset After Power Loss
shortDescription: Display shows 12:00 flashing — clock lost time after power outage.
fullDescription: Cuisinart machines do not have a battery backup, so any power loss resets the clock and disables PROG until reset.

fixSteps.title: Set clock
fixSteps.instruction: Use HOUR/MIN buttons to set current time.

fixSteps.title: Verify outlet
fixSteps.instruction: Plug into surge-protected outlet to prevent recurrence.

videoSearchQuery: Cuisinart clock reset after power outage

faq.q: Can I add a battery backup?
faq.a: No — feed via UPS or surge-protected outlet.

title: Hot Plate Stuck Off
shortDescription: Hot plate does not stay on after brewing — distinct from the auto-off pattern.
fullDescription: Hot plate may fail due to a thermal cutout trip or relay failure on the board.
symptoms: Hot plate cold to touch after brew

fixSteps.title: Wait and retry
fixSteps.instruction: Cool 30 minutes and retry.

fixSteps.title: Service
fixSteps.instruction: If still cold, hot plate or relay replacement.

whenToCallPro: If thermal cutout has permanently failed.
videoSearchQuery: Cuisinart hot plate not heating fix

faq.q: Should hot plate stay on forever?
faq.a: No — auto-off after 0-4 hours protects coffee taste.
